[[Arden, North Carolina]] | championships = Y | championship_list = *2x [[ACC Men's Basketball Tournament]] ([[2009 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2009]] & [[2010 ACC Men's Basketball Tournament|2010]]) *2010 [[NIT Season Tip-Off]] *[[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2010 NCAA]] *[[2009–10 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2009–10 ACC Men's Basketball regular season]] }} '''Miles Plumlee''' (born September 1, 1988) a [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]]/[[Center (basketball)|center]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball]] team from 2008-2012.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300170150 |title=Wake Forest Demon Deacons vs. Duke Blue Devils – Recap – January 17, 2010 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=January 17, 2010 |accessdate=March 28, 2010}}{{cite news|url=http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/acc/2009-11-12-duke-plumlee_N.htm |title=Duke's Mason Plumlee out indefinitely with broken wrist |publisher=Usatoday.Com |date=November 12, 2009 |accessdate=March 28, 2010}} As a sophomore he played in Duke's [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2010]] [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|National Championship]] winning team. ==High school== Plumlee attended high school at [[Christ School (North Carolina)|Christ School]] in [[Arden, North Carolina]], where he led the school to a 63–6 record as a junior and senior. During his high school career he was a two-time NCISAA 3A all-state team selection, an ''[[Asheville Citizen-Times]]'' All-Western North Carolina first team pick as a junior and senior. He also lettered in track as a senior and posted a school record [[high jump]] of 6’9’ showcasing his outstanding athletic abilities that he would become know for during his college basketball career. ==College== Plumlee had originally committed to play at [[Stanford University]] for the 2008-09 season, but after Stanford coach [[Trent Johnson]] left for [[Louisiana State University|LSU]] and brother [[Mason Plumlee|Mason]] had committed to play at Duke the following year, he choose to become a [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Blue Devil]], . After serving a limited role his freshman season, Plumlee earned the starting center position over senior [[Brian Zoubek]] at the beginning of the 2009–10 season before returning to a bench role later in the season. Plumlee finshed the championship winning seaon averaging 16.4 minutes per game, 4.9 rebounds and 5.2 points per game.[http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/statlines.php?playerid=2734] During the 2009-10 season Plumlee and brother Mason were often the first two players off the bench usually being brought in to games to replace Zoubek and [[Lance Thomas]].{{cite web|url=http://www2.journalnow.com/content/2010/apr/01/sticking-together/ |title=Sticking Together: Plumlee brothers finding their comfort level with Blue Devils |publisher=.journalnow.com |date= |accessdate=April 3, 2010}} Miles played a similar role in his junior campaign to that of his sophmore, contributing solid offense and defense for the team in limited playing time. He finshed the seaon averaging 17 minutes per game, 4.9 rebounds and 4.8 points. In his final season in 2011-12, Plumlee would again play the majority of the season off the bench while starting games every now and then. He went on to have his best season from a statistical view, grabbing the second most rebounds per game for the team with 7.1, behind brother Mason, as well as leading the team in field goal percentage, connecting on 61% of his shot attempts. In all Plumlee completed his four seasons at Duke having played 135 games for 654 rebounds and 650 points. {{cite web|url=http://http://goduke.statsgeek.com/basketball-m/players/statlines.php?playerid=2734|title=Duke Blue Devils Basketball Statistical Database |accessdate=June 20, 2012}} ==Family== Miles has three siblings, brothers [[Mason Plumlee|Mason]] and [[Marshall Plumlee|Marshall]] and sister Madeleine.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncaa/recruiting/basketball/mens/news/story?id=4496541 |title=Marshall Plumlee, the younger brother of Miles and Mason, is finding his own way on the court – ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=September 23, 2009 |accessdate=April 5, 2010}}{{cite news|last=Armstrong |first=Kevin |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/03/sports/ncaabasketball/03duke.html |title=After Detour, Duke’s Plumlee Brothers Arrive at Final Four |publisher=NYTimes.com |date= April 2, 2010|accessdate=April 3, 2010}} All three brothers have been involved in Duke's basketball program while Miles and younger brother Mason, are the sixth pair of brothers to play at Duke at the same time. His parents are Perky (a former [[Tennessee Technological University|Tennessee Tech]] basketball player) and Leslie (née Schultz) Plumlee (a former [[Purdue University|Purdue]] [[Purdue Boilermakers women's basketball|women's basketball]] player who set the school single-game rebound record with 25).{{cite web|url=http://www.journalgazette.net/article/20100326/SPORTS0303/303269947/1008/SPORTS
